hints: Calculate the running cumulative frequency by successively adding the frequencies for each interval.
Plot each cumulative frequency value at the UPPER boundary of its class interval: $(3, 120)$, $(4, 300)$, $(5, 500)$, $(6, 660)$, $(8, 770)$, $(10, 850)$, $(14, 900)$, beginning from $(0, 0)$.
Connect all plotted points with an increasing smooth curve or connected straight line segments.
To estimate the median time, find $\frac{N}{2} = \frac{900}{2} = 450$ on the cumulative frequency axis, read across horizontally to the curve, and then read down to the time axis.
walkthrough:
Calculate the cumulative frequencies by summing the class frequencies at each upper class boundary:
$$\begin{aligned} t \le 3 &: 120 \\ t \le 4 &: 120 + 180 = 300 \\ t \le 5 &: 300 + 200 = 500 \\ t \le 6 &: 500 + 160 = 660 \\ t \le 8 &: 660 + 110 = 770 \\ t \le 10 &: 770 + 80 = 850 \\ t \le 14 &: 850 + 50 = 900 \end{aligned}$$

Plot the cumulative frequencies at the upper class boundaries:
$$\text{Points to plot: } (3, 120), \; (4, 300), \; (5, 500), \; (6, 660), \; (8, 770), \; (10, 850), \; (14, 900)$$
Connect the points starting from $(0, 0)$ with a smooth curve or straight line segments on linear scales with clearly labelled axes.

Estimate the median time from the graph at half the total frequency:
$$\text{Median position} = \dfrac{900}{2} = 450$$
Reading across from cumulative frequency $450$ to the curve and projecting down to the horizontal time axis yields:
$$\text{Median time} = 4.8\text{ minutes} \quad (\text{accept } 4.7 \le m < 4.9)$$

ai_rubric.Constructing Cumulative-Frequency Graphs: Plot cumulative frequencies at the upper class boundaries.
ai_rubric.Reading Cumulative-Frequency Graphs: Read the median at half the total frequency from the completed graph.

teacher_walkthrough: A cumulative frequency graph shows the running total of frequencies up to each given value. For grouped continuous data, each cumulative frequency must be plotted at the upper boundary of the corresponding class interval.

Step 1: Compute the cumulative frequency by adding each class frequency to the previous total:
- Upper boundary $t = 3$: $cf = 120$
- Upper boundary $t = 4$: $cf = 120 + 180 = 300$
- Upper boundary $t = 5$: $cf = 300 + 200 = 500$
- Upper boundary $t = 6$: $cf = 500 + 160 = 660$
- Upper boundary $t = 8$: $cf = 660 + 110 = 770$
- Upper boundary $t = 10$: $cf = 770 + 80 = 850$
- Upper boundary $t = 14$: $cf = 850 + 50 = 900$

Step 2: Plot the points on the grid with time on the horizontal axis and cumulative frequency on the vertical axis:
$$(3, 120), \quad (4, 300), \quad (5, 500), \quad (6, 660), \quad (8, 770), \quad (10, 850), \quad (14, 900)$$
Start the curve at the origin $(0, 0)$ because no students took less than 0 minutes. Join all points sequentially with a smooth curve or straight lines.

Step 3: Estimate the median time. The median corresponds to the 50th percentile of the data:
$$\text{Cumulative frequency for median} = \frac{N}{2} = \frac{900}{2} = 450$$
Find 450 on the vertical axis, trace horizontally to intersect the cumulative frequency curve, and project vertically down to the time axis.
Reading this value gives $4.8$ minutes (any estimate in the range $4.7 \le m < 4.9$ is accepted).
